name: repertoire
description: Skills for coding agents: worktrees beside the checkout, reviewer lenses mined from a repo's own review history, data told so a reader gets the point and can act on it, dashboards read at a glance, thematic maps that make an honest argument about where, and prose written by Strunk's rules.

plugins.name: sidework
plugins.description: Run Claude Code tasks in git worktrees beside the main checkout (../<repo>-sidework-<session>) instead of nested inside it.

plugins.name: build-review-lens
plugins.description: Mine a repository's review history into a reviewer lens skill that reviews your branch the way its maintainer will, before the PR opens.

plugins.name: data-story
plugins.description: Turn numbers into a point a reader gets in seconds and can act on: Storytelling with Data's lessons in order, one visual picked for the reader, and the words run through write-with-style.

plugins.name: data-dashboard
plugins.description: Build, refine, and review dashboards the way Stephen Few's Information Dashboard Design teaches: one screen read at a glance, every measure against its comparison, bullet graphs and sparklines, and color only for what needs attention.

plugins.name: data-map
plugins.description: Design, build, and check thematic maps the way Slocum, Munzner, and Muehlenhaus teach: the right idiom for the data and the reader's task, an equal-area projection where area matters, classes and color computed by code, flows that curve and point, and a render a cold reader checks.

plugins.name: write-with-style
plugins.description: Write and edit prose by Strunk's The Elements of Style (1918): the point first, a topic sentence to open each paragraph, definite sentences in the active voice, and no needless words.
